analysis: Documentation-only PR. (1) New docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md (added, lines 1-100) describes an unregistered Nemotron Super image owner: in-process PNG decoder and ImageIO JPEG decode of untrusted consumer-supplied inline images. It states bounds: encoded bytes at most 64 MiB (whole body at most 8 MiB), pixel and axis caps, 500-scan JPEG cap, 1 MiB text/ICC inflate caps, CRC and zlib checks, and memory quotes (lines 72-94). It states that the owner is unregistered, which suggests no production exposure. No source code changed, so the real enforcement of these limits is unverified. The doc describes new attack surface (image parsing of consumer data on the provider, relevant to A-001/T-050/TB-007), but because it is only a description, no control regression follows. Later passes should check the actual decoder, parse bounds and the ImageIO uncancellable decode DoS if code arrives. Line 68 notes 4:2:0 saturated edges can differ from Pillow by up to 64, which is a correctness fidelity gap and not a security issue. (2) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 187 adds one sentence: a cold result returns only after the attempt's host IO refund completes. This is a lifecycle and availability clarification for the T-041 SSD cache fallback. It does not change identity binding, encryption, TTL, budget or the write cap. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. The claim is unverified against source (SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift stageTransfer and SSDCheckpointStageReservation.swift waitForRefund were not supplied). No findings.
